review_basis: Rendered comparison from actual Actions evidence: front, three-quarter, left hand

decisions.reason: Only one robust left valley; left-hand tip remains stepped, scope and local cycles unverified; measured fingers gain below Valley Sculpt c01.
Visible protruding block at distal upper hand and deformed silhouette. Highest target gain cannot compensate mesh integrity failure, one valley and worse 3/4 regression.
Two visible valleys and good global retention, but finger target gain falls strongly versus Valley Sculpt c01. Stepped distal hand contour and scope/cycle failures make it unsuitable.

learning: Reference valley count alone does not establish likeness.
A target metric can reward visually broken geometry (c02).
Local cuts on an open/face-corner GLB do not automatically create clean deformation rings.
Preserve the Valley Sculpt parent; do not chain from rejected variants.
next_hypothesis: Investigate a minimal connected quad patch around the two valley roots, anchored to measured distal boundary and preserving palm depth; validate ring closure and UV/material correspondence before bridging. Requires a new technique-specific research brief.
